evidence: polities/british-empire.json notes ('OVERLAP TO RESOLVE': same Company state, 'draw east-india-company's keyframes and ledger ... or retire this file'; its ledger agrees with the EIC ledger wherever both opened a page) and polities/east-india-company.json notes ('OVERLAP TO RESOLVE': same gains and vassal tints). The Company ruled Bengal etc. from 1757 to 1 Nov 1858 in both. EIC keyframes are direct Company rule only (about 1.94M km2 at 1858) with protected states as vassal tints in the ledger; british-empire's Cliopatria shape (3.63M km2 in 1857-58, stray Canadian cells 1788-1821) includes the protected states. Currently EIC wins 106,471 of 106,589 cell-years only because it is smaller.
fix: Keep east-india-company for its whole life 1600-1858 (direct rule shapes plus the vassal tints from its ledger). Retire british-empire's 1757-1858 shapes as a separate state (or list 'British Empire' in east-india-company cliopatria_names and drop the file; then change the counterpart strings in gwalior-state, indore-state, kingdom-of-nagpur, hyderabad-state, nawab-of-awadh, kingdom-of-mysore, sikh-empire, nepal, nawabs-of-bengal and the Rajputana dossiers). If british-empire is kept instead, its protected-state land must be drawn as vassal tint, never as direct rule.
